items.what_happened: An engine-queued solar that the hands had lost track of. At 9:00 the nano frame armnanotc_27075 (the replaced order's frame) was taken as the new solar task's frame: the created-event handler marks the builder's Build task started on any frame it makes (9:02 report: 'building a Solar Collector (armsolar) at plant2_east (C7) (not yet started)'). The 60% queue-ahead therefore fired at 9:32 on a build not begun and queued a solar at C7 (2360,5096). The real frame at 9:47 was read as that queued build beginning, so when it finished at 10:14 the task ended while the engine still held the C7 order. From 10:15 the entry read 'finishing an order'. The 10:11 list (#as2, #as4) could neither drop that order nor play its own steps, because the builder never stood idle. The engine walked the builder to C7 and laid the frame at 10:32. The builder walked off it 10:34-10:41 with no command and no enemy near, then came back and restarted the same site at 10:47 (armsolar_23071, finished 11:16).

mechanisms: Raider swarms at undefended build sites (U4, 11 frames, 458 metal: armsolar_12701, armllt_29515, armllt_23204, armsolar_29701, armllt_4438, armmex_4899, armmex_12914, armllt_28950, armmex_18665, armllt_7141, armmex_17056, plus 13 of the 23 never-started orders, whose builders died or fled): this game's Rover and Blitz swarms killed frames and builders at home and at forward extractors while the guard was away. Two parts were recoverable. (1) t2's 3:27 decision to send all of group_B west against the commander's 'keep two Blitzes at home', before the 11-armfav raid at 3:33 (armsolar_12701 and armllt_29515, 165 metal). (2) Builds started or walked into parties already in sight: the pick's 8:52 solar 480 from 4 armflash (armsolar_29701), and the list steps that walked builders into 6 and 10 armflash at G8 (armmex_12914, armmex_18665); 23 metal, plus 3 constructors that died with them.

A builder returning to its own unfinished frame starts a new one (U9 and its also, armllt_23890 and armllt_28950, 119 metal): the list re-sent 'armllt spot_70' at 7:38 at the same asked-for site, and the host's site search (Map_findClosestBuildSite) treated our standing 71% frame as an obstacle. It placed armllt_24004 64 elmos away, and the 71% frame decayed beside the working builder (armllt_23890, 60). At 8:04, the re-listed step meant as the turret under way was played as a further new Sentry, which was killed at 69% (armllt_28950, 59). Hands rule: a build whose site holds our unfinished frame of that type resumes that frame, and a step naming it is taken as done.

Orders that land on a frame without regard to it (armsolar_9171 and armllt_30702, 100 metal): t2's 'stop' flight list was written when the report showed the solar at 6% and landed 12 s later at 49%, at a site no enemy was hitting; then the builder was given away (armsolar_9171, 76; a stop result could name the frame and its share). The commander's D-gun on an armfav 30 elmos from its own frame destroyed that frame, and the report blamed 'unseen' (armllt_30702, 24; the D-gun move should keep its blast off our own frames, and the friendly-fire row should reach the fights line).

The hands' finished event ends the started build of every builder whose site is within 250 of the finished frame and of its type (pianist/mod.rs Event::UnitFinished, `def == done.def && near.dist2d(done.pos) < 250.0`, unchanged at HEAD): two advanced solars finishing beside three others turned those builders' entries to 'finishing an order' (and their progress words were the neighbour's 88-97% before that), their lists stalled, and the player stopped them as stuck at 81-97% (armadvsol_27527, _26769, _10240: 914 metal kept by matching the finished event to the builder's own frame id).

The id race and the stop/remove clash: 'armavp #avp2' on three lists made three plant frames at three places the same tick, and the player's reclaim of the two extras was cancelled a second later by the same turn's queue opening with 'stop', so both decayed instead of returning their metal (armavp_17970, armavp_6420: 208 metal; the race was fixed later in 4ed68d8, the stop-cancels-remove order is a tool semantics question).

A list's help-finish step is a repair task, which the list counts as a filler and overruns with its next step at once (lists.rs `Some(_) => true`; only reclaim steps were exempted later, 5046f71): constructor_19709's 'armmoho spot_73' step lasted one second at 17:57, so the moho the player had dropped at 25% to clear an exit lane, and meant 19709 to finish, decayed (armmoho_28891: 242 metal).

The same-tick id race: constructor_16990 and constructor_24695 played 'corvp spot_17 #vp2' in one second, each saw the id free, and both started a plant on an income of 7-11, so corvp_1291 was a second plant (285 metal, cut to about 70 had the 12:55 stop landed at once). Fixed 2026-10-12 (lists::nearest_first, same_tick_help) and unmeasured since. The id's claim still sent constructor_16990 to repair the dropped frame at 13:36.

The energy stall of 11:04-12:00: the energy store was at 0 on +130-270 a second while three Twin Guards, a nano, a refused HLT and the plant drew from the 10:04-10:40 lists. cornanotc_20410 was at 64% after 71 s; at the full rate (56 s) it would have stood by about 11:44, before the Stouts hit its builder at 11:54. cornanotc_22093 was dropped at 23% for solars because of the same stall. That is 200 metal, plus corhllt_10583 (168) marginally, about 5 s slower in its first 27 s.

Frames started into a known enemy's path with no army to cover them. The Blitz raids took cormex_1850, corllt_12691, corsolar_20037 and cormex_21827 (63 metal); two of these were list steps queued earlier that walked their builder onto a standing Blitz or were promoted while the builder was hit. party_27's Stouts at home took corhllt_10583, killed at 86% with its builder on it (168), and cornanotc_3536 (34), which a stale list step had re-sited at home instead of resuming the standing nano. That is 265 metal in all; only the 8 metal of the two queued-step frames is a hands-rule fix, and the rest needs army cover.

Same-tick id claim (H-HANDS-LISTS same_tick_help, built 2026-10-12 after this game): three '#vp2' lists landing on one tick made two plants; covers armvp_19699 (313 metal in, most of it reclaimed, plus constructor_29073's 70 s and a slower plant_16631).

Report: a builder's entry that names its list and says it waits behind the build in progress (no builder entry in this game's 63 reports names a list), and an abandoned line that gives the share when the builder left rather than when the frame vanished ('armsolar (1% built)' for an 87% solar); covers armsolar_22394 (135 metal), stopped at 83% because the player read a waiting list as one that never started.

Hands rule: a pick that walks an unhit builder off a frame a few seconds from done, against a packet that asked it to stay and fight, finishes the frame first; covers armsolar_21368 (135 metal, the commander 2 s from a finished solar) and perhaps armllt_9191 (68, about 6 s left with Stouts 4 s off).

A T2 defence frame built alone at a metal store of 0 in the path of his T2 army: armhlt_30842 (400 metal, 91%) stood 157 s at about 1% every 1-3 s, with spending equal to income and six labs producing, and an unseen Banisher killed it at 30:36-30:43; at full rate it would have stood near 30:12 (an inference). Spending priority for the defence, or a second builder on it, would have kept up to 400.

Forward extractor and turret builds left alone against lone-corgator raids for twenty minutes: the raider came during the build at spots 1,400-3,500 from home with no escort and no finished turret (armmex_6304, armmex_18847, armllt_12458, armllt_15814, armllt_1832, armllt_13591, armllt_11366, armmex_12149, armmex_12528, armllt_25508, plus the corwolv's armllt_13435 and armmex_11072: 12 frames, 317 metal). The queued help promoted by a neighbour's frame finishing: the hands' finished-event handler matches a builder's started build by type within 250 of its site, not by the frame's id, so armsolar_904 finishing 213 away made the commander leave armsolar_28188 at 98% for a guard of the plant (152 metal). Matching the finished unit to the task's own frame id would have kept it.
